R10: C8 'this branch changes no .rs file' — TRUE WHEN THE QUORUM RAN, FALSE NOW, and the refuter was the CI gate rather than a lane. The quorum receipt this round produced was refused in CI as STALE on a head the LOCAL gate passed. Root cause: scripts/quorum-gate.sh hashed `git diff` without --full-index, so git abbreviated every index line to a length chosen from the OBJECT COUNT of whichever clone ran it — this workstation (42982 objects) abbreviated to 8 and produced 3617ae6b, the clean-room runner abbreviated to 9 and produced 3d09e341, and forcing core.abbrev=9 locally reproduced the runner's hash exactly. That is forjar#573, filed as a flake ('passes on rerun'); it is per-clone deterministic and a rerun only appears to fix it when the job lands on a runner whose object count agrees with the author's. Fixed here, with a falsification test this branch wrote.

falsification.test: abbrev_independence_is_what_makes_the_binding_portable — written by THIS branch, and it is a real falsifier rather than one the cut rests on. It hashes one commit range under two core.abbrev settings and requires a single answer, and its sibling without_full_index_the_two_settings_disagree is the ANTI-VACUITY arm: it requires that WITHOUT --full-index those same two settings DISAGREE, so a test that could never have observed the bug fails loudly instead of passing quietly.
falsification.observed_failure: Removing --full-index from the diff_text= assignment in scripts/quorum-gate.sh: 'test abbrev_independence_is_what_makes_the_binding_portable ... FAILED', 'test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed' — while the anti-vacuity sibling stayed green, which is what proves the range can actually exhibit the difference. Restoring the flag returns both to ok, and the file was restored byte-identical from a copy rather than through git.

systems: Terraform: state carries terraform_version, is rewritten to the CURRENT binary's version on every state write, and a state written by a newer version is REFUSED rather than silently parsed [X] — record, refresh, enforce; forjar takes the first two and deliberately not the third, which is tracked separately as forjar#579

Kubernetes: server-side apply records metadata.managedFields, naming which manager owned which field on which operation [X], a per-field writer HISTORY rather than one name — which is the instinct behind keeping the creator in created_by instead of erasing it

SLSA, Nix, Puppet: a provenance attestation's builder.id exists to say which tool at which version produced the artifact and a consumer that cannot resolve it should reject [X]; Nix sidesteps the question entirely because the builder is part of the derivation's input closure [X]; Puppet is the weakest and most like where forjar was, carrying puppet_version in reports while the agent state is not a versioned artifact a later run reconciles against [X]
